disease_label_per_paper: Risedronate-induced chronic drug fever in Parkinson disease
presentation_summary: 85-year-old woman with Parkinson disease, depression history, multiple compression fractures, cataract surgeries, and polypharmacy was admitted for hallucinations and self-harming behavior.

She had received weekly oral risedronate 17.5 mg for osteoporosis for many years; her husband noticed her temperature had been approximately 1 degC higher than her previous normal body temperature after risedronate was started.
On admission, temperature was 37.4 degC, blood pressure 99/69 mmHg, heart rate 84/min, and oxygen saturation 95% on room air.
She had no headache, nausea, myalgia, joint swelling/tenderness/redness, respiratory symptoms, abdominal or urinary pain, skin rash, palpable lymph nodes, or heart murmur.
Blood and urine testing showed normal WBC count, CRP, transaminases, CPK, urinalysis, thyroid function, ANA, and rheumatoid factor; chest radiography showed no abnormality.

During admission she had intermittent temperatures from 36 to 38 degC despite medication reduction. Fever stopped after risedronate suspension and recurred after risedronate challenge; dechallenge and rechallenge are confirmatory/non-ranking.

underlying_or_mimic_context.condition: Parkinson disease with autonomic temperature instability as a possible mimic/context
underlying_or_mimic_context.source_text_value: Parkinson disease can have unstable body temperature due to autonomic nervous system disorder, but risedronate remained the implicated drug fever cause in the paper
the patient was receiving 14 medications and acetaminophen 600 mg/day, which might have masked fever

confirmatory_findings.finding: No infection or inflammatory source found on initial workup
confirmatory_findings.source_text_value: COVID-19 PCR negative; normal WBC, CRP, urinalysis, ANA/RF; no chest radiography abnormality
risedronate was suspended for 16 days and the fever subsided for over 16 days
after risedronate challenge, mild fever 37.2 C was observed the same evening and lasted three days

confirmatory_findings.finding: Paper diagnosis of risedronate-induced chronic fever
confirmatory_findings.source_text_value: diagnosed the patient with risedronate-induced drug fever

outcome.clinical_course: After risedronate was again suspended, she had no fever for a month and was stable at follow-up.
outcome.source_text_value: again suspended risedronate and observed for a month, after which she did not experience any fever; as of mid-January 2024 body temperature stayed in normal range

quality_warnings: Chronic/recurrent low-grade fever is included as a spectrum/context axis of simple drug fever rather than making a risedronate-specific disease leaf.
Dechallenge, rechallenge, negative workup, and paper diagnosis are non-ranking confirmatory evidence.
Parkinson disease, polypharmacy, and acetaminophen masking are preserved as context and not used as hard diagnostic labels.
